title_en: Personal status law and civil marriage in Lebanon
title_ar: الأحوال الشخصية والزواج المدني في لبنان
question_en: Which law governs marriage, divorce and family matters in Lebanon, and is civil marriage allowed?
question_ar: ما هو القانون الذي يحكم الزواج والطلاق والأحوال الشخصية في لبنان، وهل الزواج المدني مسموح؟
sub_questions: Which courts and laws decide marriage and divorce for each community?
Can two Lebanese marry in a civil ceremony inside Lebanon?
Is a civil marriage held abroad valid and registered in Lebanon?
What law applies to a Lebanese who belongs to no recognised community, or to a foreigner?
What happens to the children when a spouse changes community?
notes: There is NO enacted Lebanese civil marriage law in the database: no text creates a civil marriage ceremony or a civil family code. Only drafts exist elsewhere, so the page must say the law contains no such text. What exists: Constitution art. 9 (the state guarantees respect for the personal status system of the communities; art. 10 is only about education and community schools, so cite art. 9 for personal status). Decision 60/LR of 1936 (id 183853): art. 10 as replaced by decision 146/LR of 18 Nov 1938 (id 244457, art. 1; same wording) subjects members of recognised communities to their community's system for personal status and says Lebanese who belong to an ordinary-law community or to no community are subject to the civil law in personal status matters; foreigners follow their national law. Art. 17 and 24 of 60/LR deal with marriages concluded under another law; art. 25 says a marriage celebrated abroad in the local forms is valid, and if the spouses' personal status does not accept it, it falls under civil law in Lebanon; this is the legal basis usually cited for recognising civil marriages concluded abroad, and art. 26 of the 1951 registration law (id 197742) lets the spouse send the foreign marriage document to the nearest Lebanese consulate for registration. TRAP: decision 53/1939 (id 187138, art. 1, verified) says decisions 60 and 146 do NOT apply to Muslims and remain inapplicable to them; so the civil-law fall-back of art. 10 is not a route for Muslim spouses. Law of 2 April 1951 (id 258197): jurisdiction of the Christian and Israelite religious authorities over marriage, its validity and dissolution (art. 3); art. 16 makes void a marriage held in Lebanon before a civil authority by a Lebanese belonging to a Christian community or the Israelite community; art. 14 and 15 say which authority governs and how mixed marriages are celebrated. Not included because of the 4-law limit but existing in the database: Ottoman family rights law of 1917 (id 258195; marriage, divorce, waiting period for Sunni and Jaafari courts), Druze personal status law of 1948 (id 258196), Catholic communities law of 1949 (id 258198) and marriage law of Eastern Catholic communities (id 165615), Greek Orthodox law of 1952 (id 243809), other community codes (ids 258200, 258204, 258206, 258208, 255320), and 1930 law on jurisdiction of Islamic and Druze courts (id 177643). Custody, maintenance and divorce rules are community-specific; no single national text covers them. Do not claim that civil marriage has been performed or recognised by a court; the DB holds no judgment.

pack.why: Constitution: equality before the law; art. 9 guarantees respect for communities' personal status systems; art. 10 on community schools (not personal status)
Decision 60/LR of 1936 on communities: recognised communities, which law applies to whom, change of community, marriages under another law, marriages abroad (art. 25), liability (art. 26)
Law of 2 April 1951: jurisdiction of Christian and Israelite religious courts over betrothal, marriage, annulment, divorce; art. 16 voids civil marriage in Lebanon for them; mixed marriages
1951 law on registering personal status documents: marriage declaration to the registry within a month and registration of marriages concluded abroad via the consulate
